criteria.title: Repair use-after-free, double-free, overlap, and lifetime-escape defects.
criteria.task: Create four original local teaching defects: escape,double release,use after release and overlapping copy. State each violated property, then implement defined repairs and regressions.
criteria.purpose: A tolerated allocator error or a sanitizer crash demonstrates a repair or arbitrary code execution.

knowledge: Bound T03 topic teaching and parent project contracts
artifacts: Learner-owned PR-T03-05 implementation/notebook and fixture predictions; no assessor source

reasoning: Create four original local teaching defects: escape,double release,use after release and overlapping copy. State each violated property, then implement defined repairs and regressions.
Falsify: A tolerated allocator error or a sanitizer crash demonstrates a repair or arbitrary code execution.
State representation, pre/postconditions, ownership, failure and relevant cost assumptions rather than infer them from one run.

deliverables.D1: Prediction, exact derivation and misconception counterexample.
deliverables.D2: Create four original local teaching defects: escape,double release,use after release and overlapping copy. State each violated property, then implement defined repairs and regressions.
deliverables.D3: Independent cases, failure/diagnostic evidence and source/tool manifest for this criterion.
deliverables.D4: Change unique ownership to shared references and add a concurrent borrower; separate release accounting from access synchronization.

verification.procedure: Predict abstract lifetime violations first. Compile and run only original intentionally flawed controls in isolated local unprivileged subprocesses under ASan/UBSan with synthetic data; a negative run is expected diagnostic evidence, not a defined C output. Run repaired versions separately and verify live-only access, exactly-once cleanup and overlap-correct values. Preserve exact source/tool manifest.
verification.expected: Abstract event indices2/3 identify double-release/dead-access; repaired traces release exactly once and access only live state.
verification.pass: Meet every clause of the exact task/expected result and derive its cause; no compiler silence, crash or unrelated failure counts as proof.
verification.limits: Authoring and existing partial anchors do not establish learner performance or every execution; unavailable source/target evidence remains explicit.

security.scope: Original tiny teaching programs and learner-owned repairs only.
security.target: Four original roughly20-line C programs: block escape, double release, released access and overlapping copy.
security.environment: Local unprivileged disposable subprocesses under sanitizers; synthetic values only.
security.attacker_capabilities: Select a documented operation sequence or length in the original teaching program; no third-party binaries or external target access.
security.isolation: No network, credentials, elevated privileges or production inputs; separate subprocess per undefined-behavior control.
security.exposing_transition: Use after scope/release; release a second time; submit intersecting source and destination ranges to a disjoint-copy contract.
security.exploitability_limits: A diagnostic or crash demonstrates only the observed bounded violation; no arbitrary code execution or privilege claim.
security.success_condition: Expected sanitizer observation or abstract resource-state rejection in the teaching target; repairs produce correct values and exactly-once release.
security.repair: Replace escaped storage with caller-owned storage; enforce ownership state; route overlap to a permitted movement algorithm.
security.regression: Repeat the four exposing sequences and add empty, adjacent, singleton and failure-cleanup cases to repaired programs.
security.residual_limits: Sanitizer coverage is execution-dependent and cannot prove all invalid executions absent; concurrency requires a separate synchronization argument.
